entities.name: Ferdinand August of Lobkowicz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ferdinand August Leopold von Lobkowicz (1659–1715), the 3rd Prince of Lobkowicz and Duke of Sagan, epitomized the powerful Bohemian aristocracy within the Holy Roman Empire during the late 17th and early 18th centuries. As a prominent statesman and diplomat, he served two Habsburg emperors, Leopold I and Joseph I, navigating the complex political landscape of Central Europe during an era marked by dynastic rivalries, particularly with France, and the ongoing consolidation of Habsburg power. His career reflects the intricate interplay between aristocratic influence, imperial service, and the defense of hereditary lands within a sprawling, multi-ethnic empire, solidifying the Lobkowicz family's position as one of the most influential noble houses.

His political career ascended rapidly, culminating in his appointment as President of the Imperial Court Council (Reichshofrat) in 1709, one of the highest judicial and administrative bodies of the Holy Roman Empire. Prior to this, from 1707, he served as the Imperial Principal Commissioner at the Perpetual Diet of Regensburg, the central legislative assembly, where he represented the Emperor's interests amidst the numerous estates of the Empire. These roles placed him at the heart of imperial governance, influencing legal decisions, administrative policy, and diplomatic negotiations crucial to maintaining the Habsburg monarchy's authority and prestige, especially during the War of the Spanish Succession (1701-1714).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ferdinand August of Lobkowicz held high imperial offices, including President of the Reichshofrat, contributing to the administrative and judicial stability of the Holy Roman Empire during a period of significant geopolitical flux. His career exemplifies the enduring power of dynastic service and aristocratic influence in shaping Central European politics.
